title: Characterizing elusive, faint dusty star-forming galaxies: a lensed, optically undetected ALMA galaxy at z   3.3
question: What are the physical properties (redshift, stellar mass, SFR, dust mass, magnification) of a serendipitously detected, optically undetected, lensed faint submm galaxy at z~3.3 in COSMOS, and is it representative of elusive dust-obscured star-forming galaxies missing from the cosmic SFH census?

data.arrays: 12 m antennae (32 and 39 in the two runs)

what.value: UltraVISTA-DR1 Ks-selected catalogue photometry (30 bands) used for target selection

evidence.quote: on the photometry from the UltraVISTA-DR1 $\rm K_s$–selected catalogue of (cite: muzzin13) (30 photometric bands)
spectroscopic redshift of $z$=1.1458 (from the Nov. 2015 zCOSMOS release, (cite: lilly09))

what.value: VLA 20 cm radio flux of the counterpart

evidence.quote: In the 20 cm VLA catalogue of (cite: bondi08) we found a radio counterpart of our faint SMG
we looked for X-ray counterparts in the *Chandra* catalogue of (cite: civano16) but found none

what.value: Main Sequence template used to model the lens FIR emission

evidence.quote: We assumed that the optical galaxy can be described by the Main Sequence template of (cite: elbaz11)

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA continuum flux and size
recipe.method: Gaussian model fit directly to visibilities with uvmodelfit; checked by image-plane Gaussian fit deconvolved from beam
Ks-band detection with SExtractor; template-fitting photometry with T-PHOT using I814 priors (Ks priors for IRAC); HST flux scaled via colour
assumptions: ALMA source treated as point-like at Ks position in I814 prior

recipe.method: SED fit I814-IRAC with PEGASE 2.0 templates; stellar mass from BC03 with exponentially declining SFH at best-fit z
assumptions: Chabrier IMF; LCDM H0=70, Om=0.3, OL=0.7

recipe.goal: Deblend FIR fluxes and derive IR luminosity
recipe.method: Assume 24um and part of Herschel flux belongs to lens (Elbaz Main Sequence template), subtract from Herschel photometry, iterate with Draine&Li fit (4 iterations); fit SMG templates of Michalowski10 and Pope08; adopt mean and dispersion of L_IR
key_parameters: 35% uncertainty on model added in quadrature
assumptions: All 24um emission initially attributed to the optical lens

recipe.method: SFR_IR+UV = 1e-10 L_bol with L_bol = 2.2 L_UV + L_IR; radio SFR via Barger12; dust mass from Draine&Li fit and modified blackbody (beta=2)
key_parameters: kappa at 240um 5.17 cm2/g; 100um band excluded from MBB fit

recipe.method: Singular isothermal sphere lens with velocity dispersion from Tully-Fisher relation at z~1 (Tiley16), distribution of mu; +10% for ellipticity correction

evidence.quote: The integrated flux over the source is $3.90 \pm 0.41$ mJy
We infer a photometric redshift of 3.28
translates into an SFR estimate of $237 \pm 41 M_\odot/yr$
gives a dust mass of $M_{dust}=1.12^{+0.16}_{-0.08} \cdot 10^9 M_\odot$
We therefore adopted a value of $1.54$ as an estimate of the magnification factor.
is between 2 and 3.8 (depending on the adopted SFR tracer)

not_stated_but_needed: Briggs robust value, cell size, image size and masking for clean
Which UltraVISTA/other files and cutouts exactly used; SExtractor parameter values
uvmodelfit starting parameters and spw/channel selection for continuum
Details of the lens model input (rotation velocity-K-band relation numbers) and the Monte Carlo realisation count
Full PEGASE/BC03 grid parameters (depends on Santini15 Table 1)
How the Herschel 100 micron upper limit was set in T-PHOT
missing_for_reproduction: Briggs robust, image size and cell
score_reason: ALMA data public and flux measurement simple, but SED/deblending analysis relies on external imaging, catalogs and unspecified parameters.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, simple uvmodelfit flux and size measurement gives numeric result 3.90+-0.41 mJy.
